prompt: What is the first thing to do with a slow pipeline?

choices.text: Buy a faster machine
choices.why: That comes last, if at all.

choices.text: Find out where the time goes
Add an index to every column
Rewrite it in another tool, since the one in use is probably the reason it is slow

prompt: Match each instrument to what it reports.

pairs.right: The route the database took, and the rows

prompt: Why is one INSERT per row so much slower than COPY for the same rows?

choices.text: INSERT checks every constraint on the table and COPY skips them
INSERT compresses the data before it reaches the table
COPY skips the transaction
choices.why: All three ran in one transaction.

choices.text: Each row is a round trip between client and server

prompt: Roughly how many times faster was COPY than one INSERT per row, in the recording? Round to the nearest ten.
Why did the timing script put all three methods inside one transaction?

choices.text: COPY requires it
To roll back the rows afterwards, leaving the table as it was
So the slow method is not made slower by a commit per row
choices.why: Right. The comparison is about round trips.

choices.text: Temporary tables need a transaction around each write to them

prompt: What does the made-up large table keep from the real data?

choices.text: Its shape: days, shops and books in the same mix
choices.why: Right. So what holds for reading it holds for a real table.

choices.text: Real sales from six years
choices.why: The copies are not real sales.

choices.text: Nothing; it is random
choices.why: It is copied from the real table.

choices.text: Only the March rows

prompt: How many lines did the 16th have in the large table?
Without an index, why does finding one day take longer as the table grows?

choices.text: Every row of the table is read to find it
The day has more lines each year as the shop grows
The planner gets slower
DELETE locks the whole table while it looks for the rows
choices.why: Locking was not what took the time.

prompt: What does an index on `order_date` cost the nightly load?

choices.text: Nothing; indexes only help
choices.why: Every insert also writes the index.

choices.text: It forbids deletes on the table
Every insert also writes to the index
choices.why: Right. Space, and time during the load.

choices.text: It must be rebuilt by hand every night
choices.why: PostgreSQL keeps it up to date.

prompt: In the plan without an index, PostgreSQL read every row: a `___ Scan`.
Why does the gap between a full rebuild and a 30-day window widen every year?
hint: Which one grows with the table?

choices.text: The window gets slower each year
PostgreSQL slows down with age
Indexes stop working on old data
One grows with the table; the other stays at thirty days
choices.why: Right. History only adds to one side.

prompt: What does the window give up in exchange for its speed?

choices.text: Idempotency, because a second run now writes the month twice
Changes older than the window, which need a full rebuild
choices.why: Right. The drift test says when.

choices.text: The index
choices.why: The index is what makes it fast.

choices.text: Transactions

prompt: How many pages did the query for March read through the index?
Why does asking for fewer columns save little in PostgreSQL and a lot in a columnar warehouse?

choices.text: PostgreSQL compresses columns
Columnar warehouses keep no indexes, so every query reads each column in full
PostgreSQL stores rows together; a columnar store, each column apart
choices.why: Right. Reading one column there skips the rest.

choices.text: PostgreSQL ignores the select list and reads every column of each row

prompt: Why should the morning report read `daily_sales` rather than `fact_sales`?

choices.text: It is a small summary; the report reads far less
choices.why: Right. That ratio is the point of a mart.

choices.text: fact_sales is wrong
daily_sales has an index
choices.why: It is small; that is the reason.

choices.text: Reports cannot read incremental models

prompt: Order the steps for a pipeline that is too slow.
items: Change the costliest thing the measurement found

prompt: Which of these savings has a price somewhere else? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: An index on the date
A 30-day window
A mart for the reports
choices.why: Right. One more thing to keep right.

choices.text: Measuring first
choices.why: That costs a few minutes and saves the rest.

prompt: A loader writes a million rows a night with one INSERT per row and takes two hours. What is the first change to try?

choices.text: A bigger server
choices.why: The time is in round trips, not in the server.

choices.text: Load every other night
choices.why: That halves freshness, not the work per row.

choices.text: Add more indexes to the target table
Write with COPY
choices.why: Right. One stream instead of a million conversations.
